clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Mann-Whitney U Test (for group comparisons of mean deviations); Permutation Analysis of Linear Models (PALM) (for group differences in normative deviation maps); Spearman correlations (between deviations and aggression factor); Logistic regression (to predict DBD diagnosis from ICA components); Mann-Whitney U test (for differences in ICA components between cases and controls). Linked ICA components predicted 23% of the variance of DBD. Component 8 explained 9% of the variance in the aggression factor.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study found aberrant age-related brain deviations in DBD, particularly in the amygdala, and that multimodal integration of deviation patterns identified the DMN, striatum, and amygdala as neural signatures associated with aggression.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: DBD cases showed increased age-related brain deviations, particularly positive deviations in functional measures, with significant group differences in regional deviations in the parahippocampal gyrus/amygdala, fusiform gyrus, middle temporal gyrus, and cuneus for negative faces. Deviations from positive/neutral face processing were significantly associated with aggression (ρ = 0.24, pFDR = 0.036). Multimodal integration of functional and anatomical deviations explained 23% of the variance in DBD phenotype. A specific multimodal component (component 8), predominantly reflecting positive/neutral face and shape processing deviations, was significantly associated with the aggression factor (pFDR = 0.02) and explained 9% of its variance, highlighting the DMN, striatum, and amygdala as key neural signatures.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study combined normative modeling to map individual deviations from typical age-related patterns and linked independent component analysis (LICA) to integrate subject-specific deviations from multiple modalities, aiming for individualized inferences in precision medicine.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limitations include relatively small sample size for normative modeling (especially for TD-only models), inability to distinguish between early-onset and adolescent-onset DBD, insufficient power to statistically test sex differences, cross-sectional study design limiting inferences about neurodevelopmental trajectories, potential dilution of subtle effects due to the task design, and heterogeneity of the DBD group due to inclusion criteria.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Exclusion criteria included MRI contraindications, IQ<80, and primary DSM-5 diagnosis of psychosis, bipolar disorder, major depression, or anxiety disorder.
